```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
survey <- read_csv("data/survey_attitudes.csv") |>
  mutate(
    high_support = support_international_cooperation >= 7,
    high_threat = perceived_security_threat >= 6
  )
```

# Unconditional vs conditional

```{r}
p_high <- mean(survey$high_support)
p_high

survey |>
  filter(education == "Postgraduate") |>
  summarise(p_high_given_postgrad = mean(high_support))
```

**Interpret:** conditioning on postgraduate education changes the reference group.

# Conditioning on high threat

```{r}
survey |>
  filter(high_threat) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    p_high_support = mean(high_support)
  )
```

# Check the definition $P(A\cap B)/P(B)$

```{r}
p_both <- mean(survey$high_support & survey$high_threat)
p_threat <- mean(survey$high_threat)
p_both / p_threat
```

Should match the filtered mean above (up to rounding).

# Independence quick look

```{r}
p_high * p_threat
p_both
```

If these differ, high support and high threat are associated in this sample — **not** a causal claim.
